service:
Amazon EventBridge Custom Event Bus

Amazon EventBridge event bus API. An event bus receives events published by your applications and AWS services, stores them for a configurable retention period, and delivers them to subscribers. A subscriber filters events, optionally transforms them, and invokes a target such as Lambda, SQS, SNS, Kinesis, Step Functions, or an HTTP endpoint. The API manages event buses, subscribers, event sources, resource policies, and tags, and publishes events through PutEvents and PutRawEvents.

operations.CreateEventBus: Creates an event bus. Provisioning is asynchronous: the bus is returned in the CREATING state and transitions to ACTIVE when ready (see the EventBusActive waiter). Retries carrying the same ClientToken are idempotent.
operations.CreateEventSource: Creates an EventSource, which forwards events from an origin (an AWS service, a partner, or a third-party webhook provider) to an event bus. The event bus must be in the ACTIVE state. This operation is idempotent: retries that use the same ClientToken return the same result.
operations.CreateSubscriber: Creates a subscriber on an event bus, which delivers matching events to the configured target. The bus must be ACTIVE. Retries carrying the same ClientToken are idempotent. A subscriber that targets an Amazon MSK cluster provisions its connectivity asynchronously after this call returns and begins delivering when its ConnectivityState reaches ACTIVE (see the MskSubscriberActive waiter).
operations.DeleteEventBus: Deletes an event bus. Deletion is asynchronous: the bus moves to DELETING and disappears when complete (see the EventBusDeleted waiter). A bus with subscribers or event sources cannot be deleted.
operations.DeleteEventSource: Deletes an EventSource. Forwarding from its origin stops.
operations.DeleteResourcePolicy: Deletes the named resource policy attached to an event bus.
operations.DeleteSubscriber: Deletes a subscriber. Events are no longer delivered to its target.
operations.DescribeEventBus: Returns the full configuration and lifecycle state of an event bus.
operations.DescribeEventSource: Returns the full configuration and lifecycle state of an EventSource.
operations.DescribeSubscriber: Returns the full configuration and state of a subscriber.
operations.GetResourcePolicy: Returns the named resource policy attached to an event bus. Fails with ResourceNotFoundException when the event bus or the named policy does not exist.
operations.ListEventBuses: Lists the event buses visible to the caller: buses the account owns and buses shared with it through AWS RAM. Shared entries carry identity fields only (Name, EventBusArn, EventBusAccountId); owned entries carry every summary field. Set EventBusAccountId to scope the list to one owner account.
operations.ListEventSources: Lists EventSources as summaries. By default the list spans the EventSources the caller account owns; set EventBusArn to scope it to one bus. Use DescribeEventSource to retrieve full configuration.
operations.ListResourcePolicies: Lists the resource policies attached to an event bus as summaries (policy name and revision ID). Use GetResourcePolicy to retrieve a policy document.
operations.ListSubscribers: Lists subscribers as summaries. By default the list spans the subscribers the caller account owns across all buses; set EventBusArn to scope it to one bus. Use DescribeSubscriber to retrieve full configuration.
operations.ListTagsForResource: Lists the tags on an event bus, subscriber, or event source.
operations.PutEvents:
Publishes events to an event bus.

The total size of all event entries in a request must not exceed 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes). The limit applies to the request as a whole, not to individual entries. If you exceed the limit, the request fails with InvalidInputException and the service publishes none of the entries in the request.
operations.PutRawEvents:
Publishes pre-shaped events to an event bus.

The total size of all event entries in a request must not exceed 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes), including the Data payload and the keys and values of Metadata for each entry. The limit applies to the request as a whole, not to individual entries.

If you exceed the limit, the request fails with InvalidInputException, and the service doesn't publish any of the entries in the request.
operations.PutResourcePolicy: Attaches a named resource policy to an event bus — the only resource type that supports policies; other resource ARNs are rejected. Each bus holds two named policies: "default" (customer-managed, full IAM policy language including Deny) and "AWS_RAM" (written exclusively by AWS Resource Access Manager to reflect resource shares). Both policies are evaluated on cross-account authorization; an explicit Deny in either overrides an Allow in the other. Operations that omit PolicyName target "default". A "default" policy that would grant public access is rejected with PublicPolicyException and is not attached; this check is always on and cannot be disabled.
operations.RevokeResource: Revokes a subscriber or an EventSource. The bus owner calls this to withdraw a misbehaving resource attached to their bus. Revocation is terminal: there is no operation that clears it. A revoked resource refuses mutating operations with InvalidStateException; delete stays available for cleanup.
operations.RotateWebhookCredentials:
Sets a new credential on a webhook EventSource. If you supply Credential, EventBridge uses that value. Otherwise, EventBridge generates one. For HTTP Basic authentication, only the password changes. The username does not change. EventBridge never returns the credential. To read a generated value, call secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the secret that SecretArn identifies.

You can rotate the credential of an EventSource in the ACTIVE, UPDATING, or UPDATE_FAILED state. For a revoked EventSource or an EventSource in any other state, EventBridge returns InvalidStateException. EventBridge also returns InvalidStateException if the secret of the EventSource is scheduled for deletion or has been deleted.

If you rotate the credential of one EventSource too many times in 24 hours, EventBridge returns LimitExceededException. Retry later. The limit becomes available again automatically.

If AWS Secrets Manager throttles the call, EventBridge returns ThrottlingException. Retry later.

To use this operation, you must have the following permissions in your IAM policy:

  • secretsmanager:PutSecretValue on the secret of the EventSource

  • secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the secret of the EventSource, for HTTP Basic authentication only

  • kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt on the AWS KMS key that encrypts the secret

The resource policy of the secret must not deny the secretsmanager actions.

EventBridge accepts the new credential when this call returns. In rare cases, the new credential takes up to 2 minutes to reach every EventBridge endpoint.

EventBridge also accepts the previous credential for 15 minutes after the rotation. The window ends at the CreatedDate of the AWSCURRENT secret version plus 15 minutes. Only the credential that the most recent rotation replaced stays valid. If you rotate again within 15 minutes, the older credential stops working immediately.

A retry with the same ClientToken within 8 hours returns the same result and does not rotate again. A retry of a rotation that supplied a value can arrive after a later rotation completed. In that case, the retried value becomes the current credential, and the credential it replaces does not stay valid.
operations.TagResource: Adds or replaces tags on an event bus, subscriber, or event source.
operations.UntagResource: Removes tags from an event bus, subscriber, or event source.
operations.UpdateEventBus: Updates an event bus. The update is asynchronous: the bus moves to UPDATING and returns to ACTIVE when the change is applied. Fields omitted from the request are left unchanged.
operations.UpdateEventSource: Updates an EventSource. Fields omitted from the request are left unchanged.
operations.UpdateSubscriber: Updates a subscriber. Fields omitted from the request are left unchanged. Changing an Amazon MSK subscriber's connectivity can re-provision it; when it does, the subscriber resumes delivering once its ConnectivityState returns to ACTIVE (see the MskSubscriberActive waiter).

BatchConfigurationMaxBatchSizeInteger.base: Nullable integer — no default, absence means "not set".

refs.BatchConfiguration$MaxBatchSize: The maximum number of events to include in a single batch delivered to the target. The service delivers up to this many events per batch; fewer may be delivered when the batch window elapses or the target's per-batch limit is smaller. This is a maximum, not a guaranteed count. Valid range is 1-500 (default: 10, or the target API's per-batch maximum). The resolved value applied by the service is returned on read.

This is a maximum; a batch may be delivered sooner if it reaches MaxBatchSize or another delivery condition is met. Valid range is 0-300 (default: 0, meaning no wait). The resolved value applied by the service is always returned on read.

BusState.base:
Lifecycle state of an event bus.

  • CREATING: Bus creation is in progress.

  • CREATE_FAILED: Bus creation failed; see StateReason. The bus cannot be recovered or recreated in place: delete it with DeleteEventBus, then create a new bus.

  • ACTIVE: Bus is fully operational and can accept events.

  • UPDATING: Bus update is in progress.

  • UPDATE_FAILED: Bus update failed; the bus remains operational with its previous configuration.

  • DELETING: Bus deletion is actively in progress.

  • DELETE_FAILED: Bus deletion failed; see StateReason. Retry DeleteEventBus after removing subscribers and event sources.

ConcurrentModificationException.base: Another change to the resource is already in progress. Retry the request.

ConflictException.base:
A client-supplied precondition (e.g. ExpectedRevisionId on a resource-policy write) did not match the current state of the resource. Retrying the same request will fail again; re-read the resource and re-evaluate before retrying.

A conditional request is not retry-safe on its own. If an earlier attempt committed but its response never reached the caller, retrying fails with this error, which is indistinguishable from another writer having won. Compare the resource's current contents with what the request intended: a successful attempt stores a revision ID the caller never saw, so the revision alone cannot tell the two apart, but matching contents mean the change took effect.

ConnectivityState.base: Provisioning state of the connectivity EventBridge sets up between a subscriber and its target cluster. Covers all of that setup (for PRIVATE connectivity: the VPC connection, DNS records, and related resources), so it can lag the state the target service reports for the VPC connection. Distinct from the customer-controlled subscriber State (RUNNING/STOPPED). PROVISIONING: provisioning is in progress. PROVISION_FAILED: provisioning failed; see StateReason. DeadLetterQueueArn.base: The ARN of the destination that receives events that could not be delivered. An Amazon SQS queue is the supported destination. The queue-name grammar mirrors SQS's own rule: 1-80 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-], where a FIFO name's ".fifo" suffix counts toward the 80 (so a FIFO base name is at most 75 chars). Shared: both the subscriber's and the EventSource's OnFailureConfiguration point at it.

refs.OnFailureConfiguration$Arn: The ARN of the destination that receives events that could not be delivered. An Amazon SQS queue is the supported destination.

refs.MskDetails$StateReason: Why provisioning failed. Present only when ConnectivityState is PROVISION_FAILED.
refs.UpdateEventBusResponse$StateReason: Human-readable explanation of why an event bus is in its current State. Omitted when the bus is in a normal operational state (ACTIVE). refs.StepFunctionsParameters$TraceHeader: X-Ray trace header for distributed tracing. Accepts JSONata expression.

refs.SqsMessageAttributeValue$StringValue: String attribute value. A JSONata expression resolves once per delivered event.

VpcConnectionArn.base: ARN of a VPC connection EventBridge creates to an Amazon MSK cluster. EventBridge owns the connection, so the account in the ARN is an EventBridge account, not the caller's.

refs.MskDetails$VpcConnectionArn: ARN of the VPC connection EventBridge uses to reach the cluster. Present only for PRIVATE connectivity, once the connection exists. It is the connection the cluster owner sees through the MSK ListClientVpcConnections API.

WebhookAuthConfiguration.base: How the provider authenticates its webhook requests. Exactly one variant must be set.

refs.WebhookEventsSourceConfiguration$AuthCon: How the provider authenticates its requests. Exactly one authentication type must be set, and it can't be changed after the EventSource is created.

WebhookBasicHttpAuthConfiguration.base: The provider sends HTTP Basic authentication credentials: an Authorization header with the value "Basic " followed by the Base64 encoding of username:password. Supply both Username and Password, or omit both so that EventBridge generates the pair. Supplying only one fails with InvalidInputException. EventBridge stores both only in AWS Secrets Manager and never returns them, including from DescribeEventSource.

WebhookCredential.base: A new webhook credential. Exactly one variant must be set.

refs.RotateWebhookCredentialsRequest$Credenti: The new credential. Set the member that matches the authentication type of the EventSource. If you set a member that does not match the authentication type, EventBridge returns InvalidInputException. If you omit Credential, EventBridge generates a value.

WebhookDeduplicationConfiguration.base: Deduplication settings for a webhook EventSource's events.

refs.WebhookEventsSourceConfiguration$Dedupli: Optional. Deduplicates this EventSource's events on the event bus. Omit it to deduplicate nothing.

WebhookDeduplicationType.base: How duplicate events are detected. Deduplicating by a caller-supplied ID is not available for a webhook EventSource, because its sender calls an HTTP endpoint and so cannot set an ID per event.

WebhookDelimiter.base: The separator between parts of a header value.

refs.WebhookHmacAuthConfiguration$Delimiter: The separator between parts of the signature header value, for example a comma for a header value of t=1727816400,v1=<signature>, or a space when the header carries several signatures. Required when TimestampHttpHeader is the same header as SignatureHttpHeader.

WebhookDetails.base: Values EventBridge generated for a webhook EventSource.

WebhookEventsSourceConfiguration.base: Configuration for receiving events from an external provider, such as a SaaS application, that sends them as HTTPS POST requests to a webhook URL. The provider authenticates with an HTTP scheme instead of AWS credentials.

refs.EventSourceConfiguration$WebhookEventsCo: Configuration for receiving events that a third-party provider sends to an HTTPS webhook URL.

WebhookHeaderName.base: The name of an HTTP header. Must be a valid header name as defined in RFC 7230.

refs.WebhookHmacAuthConfiguration$SignatureHt: The name of the header that carries the signature, for example X-Hub-Signature-256. When TimestampHttpHeader names the same header, Delimiter, SignaturePrefix and TimestampPrefix are all required. Reserved names are rejected, as described on StaticTokenAuthConfiguration's TokenHttpHeader.
refs.WebhookHmacAuthConfiguration$TimestampHt: The name of the header that carries the request timestamp. Required when SignedMessageComposition is TIMESTAMP_DOT_BODY or MESSAGE_ID_DOT_TIMESTAMP_DOT_BODY, or when TimestampToleranceInSeconds is set. Not allowed when SignedMessageComposition is BODY, because BODY does not sign the timestamp. Reserved names are rejected, as described on StaticTokenAuthConfiguration's TokenHttpHeader.
refs.WebhookHmacAuthConfiguration$MessageIdHt: The name of the header that carries the message ID. Required when SignedMessageComposition is MESSAGE_ID_DOT_TIMESTAMP_DOT_BODY. Requests whose message ID contains a period (.) are rejected. Reserved names are rejected, as described on StaticTokenAuthConfiguration's TokenHttpHeader.
refs.WebhookStaticTokenAuthConfiguration$Toke: The name of the header that carries the secret, for example X-Webhook-Secret. Reserved names are rejected: the names EventBridge's edge writes, such as Host and the X-Forwarded-* family, and the hop-by-hop and framing names an HTTP intermediary may rewrite, such as Connection and Content-Length. Authorization is allowed.

WebhookHmacAlgorithm.base: Hash algorithms supported for hash-based message authentication code (HMAC) signatures.

refs.WebhookHmacAuthConfiguration$Algorithm: The hash algorithm the provider uses to compute the signature.

WebhookHmacAuthConfiguration.base: The provider signs each request with a hash-based message authentication code (HMAC) of the secret. Amazon EventBridge accepts the request if any signature in SignatureHttpHeader matches.

refs.WebhookAuthConfiguration$HmacAuthConfigu: The provider signs each request with an HMAC of the secret.

refs.WebhookHmacAuthConfiguration$Encoding: How the provider encodes the signature in the header.

WebhookMetadataHttpHeaderList.base: The HTTP request headers to add to event metadata.

refs.WebhookEventsSourceConfiguration$Metadat: The HTTP request headers to add to each event's metadata, up to 20. Header names are case-insensitive and can't repeat. Each header is added under its lowercase name. Omit the list to add no headers. Headers that carry credentials or that describe the network path, and the header that carries the static token, can't be listed.

WebhookMetadataHttpHeaderName.base: The name of an HTTP request header to add to event metadata. Must be a valid header name as defined in RFC 7230.

WebhookSecretArn.base: The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that holds a webhook EventSource's secret.

refs.RotateWebhookCredentialsResponse$SecretA: The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that holds the credential. It doesn't change when the credential is rotated.
refs.WebhookDetails$SecretArn: The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret, in your account, that holds the secret.

refs.WebhookHmacAuthConfiguration$SecretEncod: How the secret is encoded. RAW uses the secret's characters as the signing key. BASE64 decodes the secret first, as providers that follow the Standard Webhooks specification require. The default is RAW.

WebhookSecretValue.base: The secret a provider uses to authenticate webhook requests.

refs.WebhookCredential$StaticTokenSecretValue: The new token for static token authentication.
refs.WebhookCredential$BasicHttpPassword: The new password for HTTP Basic authentication. The username does not change.
refs.WebhookCredential$HmacSecretValue: The new HMAC secret, in the SecretEncoding of the EventSource. With BASE64, EventBridge removes a leading "whsec_". The key must be 16 to 512 bytes; with BASE64 SecretEncoding, this is measured after decoding.
refs.WebhookHmacAuthConfiguration$SecretValue: The signing key shared with the provider. If you omit it, EventBridge generates one. EventBridge stores the key only in AWS Secrets Manager and never returns it, including from DescribeEventSource. The key must be 16 to 512 bytes; with BASE64 SecretEncoding, this is measured after decoding.
refs.WebhookStaticTokenAuthConfiguration$Secr: The token the provider sends in the header. If you omit it, EventBridge generates one. EventBridge stores the token only in AWS Secrets Manager and never returns it, including from DescribeEventSource. EventBridge compares it against the entire header value, so a provider that sends Authorization: Bearer <token> needs SecretValue to include the "Bearer " prefix.

WebhookSignaturePrefix.base: The text that precedes the signature in a header value.

refs.WebhookHmacAuthConfiguration$SignaturePr: The text that precedes the signature in the header value, for example sha256=. Required when TimestampHttpHeader is the same header as SignatureHttpHeader.

WebhookSignedMessageComposition.base:
How the provider assembles the message it signs from the request.

  • BODY - The request body alone. BODY provides no replay protection.

  • TIMESTAMP_DOT_BODY - <timestamp>.<body>. Requires TimestampHttpHeader.

  • MESSAGE_ID_DOT_TIMESTAMP_DOT_BODY - <messageId>.<timestamp>.<body>, as in the Standard Webhooks specification. Requires TimestampHttpHeader and MessageIdHttpHeader.

refs.WebhookHmacAuthConfiguration$SignedMessa:
How the provider assembles the message it signs from the request.

  • BODY - The request body alone. BODY provides no replay protection.

  • TIMESTAMP_DOT_BODY - <timestamp>.<body>. Requires TimestampHttpHeader.

  • MESSAGE_ID_DOT_TIMESTAMP_DOT_BODY - <messageId>.<timestamp>.<body>, as in the Standard Webhooks specification. Requires TimestampHttpHeader and MessageIdHttpHeader.

WebhookStaticTokenAuthConfiguration.base: The provider sends the secret as the value of an HTTP header.

refs.WebhookAuthConfiguration$StaticTokenAuth: The provider sends a static token in an HTTP header.

WebhookTimestampPrefix.base: The text that precedes the timestamp in a header value.

refs.WebhookHmacAuthConfiguration$TimestampPr: The text that precedes the timestamp in the header value, for example t=. Required when TimestampHttpHeader is the same header as SignatureHttpHeader.

WebhookTimestampToleranceInSeconds.base: The maximum allowed difference, in seconds, between a request's timestamp and its receipt.

refs.WebhookHmacAuthConfiguration$TimestampTo: The maximum difference, in seconds, allowed between the request timestamp and the time EventBridge receives the request. Requests outside this window are rejected. The default is 300 seconds. Requires TimestampHttpHeader. Not allowed when SignedMessageComposition is BODY, because BODY does not sign the timestamp.

WebhookUrl.base: The HTTPS URL a provider sends webhook requests to.

refs.WebhookDetails$WebhookUrl: The HTTPS URL to configure in the provider. The URL doesn't change for the life of the EventSource.

WebhookUsername.base: The username for HTTP Basic authentication. Can't contain a colon or whitespace.
